sections.title: A Song of Salvation
observations: This chapter begins with a song that celebrates the salvation and strength of God. The imagery of a strong city reflects the security and peace that God provides to His people. The mention of 'walls and bulwarks' signifies divine protection against enemies.

sections.title: The Way of the Righteous
observations: The focus shifts to the characteristics of the righteous. They are described as those who keep their minds steadfast on God, trusting in Him. This highlights the importance of faith and reliance on God for peace.

sections.title: The Judgment of the Wicked
observations: The chapter contrasts the fate of the righteous with that of the wicked. The wicked are depicted as those who do not seek God and will ultimately face judgment. This serves as a warning about the consequences of rejecting God's ways.

sections.title: A Call to Trust in God
observations: The final verses encourage the people to trust in God, especially in times of trouble. The assurance of God's faithfulness and the promise of resurrection provide hope for the faithful.

importantVerses.commentary: You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are steadfast, because they trust in you.
But your dead will live, Lord; their bodies will rise—let those who dwell in the dust wake up and shout for joy.

questions: What does it mean to have a mind that is steadfast on God?
How does the imagery of a strong city relate to our understanding of God's protection?
In what ways can we apply the call to trust in God during our own times of trouble?
What implications does the promise of resurrection have for believers today?
